newsitem.title: UK: Emerging market debt lower but Bulgaria higher.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt lower but Bulgaria higher.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mostly lower on Wednesday but Bulgarian Brady bonds bucked the trend, posting gains following news that the country's parliament elected a new Central Bank governor, traders said.
"Bulgaria has taken off again this morning. It is very popular and there aren't a lot of people selling into this," said one Brady trader at U.S. investment bank in London.

Earlier today, Bulgaria's parliament elected Svetoslav Gavriiski to head the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB), which will operate under a currency board system that will be launched on July 1 to stabilise the economy.
Bulgarian IABs were 1/4 firmer at 69-1/8 bid and its FLRB's were 1/8 stronger at 53-3/4 bid.

Even though the economic fundamentals of many emerging market countries remains strong, market experts said investors continued to keep a close watch on movements in dollar/yen and the U.S. Treasury and stock markets.
"We are seeing people buying and there is more money coming in every moment but at the same time there is some hesitancy in a sense of how much further it can go," said a trader.
"We are long and we intend to stay long because at the end Of the day there is value here in our markets but the rest of the world is a little bit worrying," the trader added.
Market specialists said volume remained thin, however, ahead of May U.S. retail sales on Thursday and May U.S. producer prices on Friday.
"People are generally quite bullish but...the market is a bit toppy," said one trader.

In the Latin Brady market, Argentine FRBs were 1/8 higher at 93-3/4, Brazilian "C" bonds were 1/4 lower at 79-5/8 and Mexican pars were 1/8 weaker at 76-3/8 bid. -- Diane Craft, London Newsroom +44 171 542-5110
